german_span: die erste Frau (<ab>acc.</ab>) durch eine zweite Frau (<ab>instr.</ab>) hintansetzen
current_russian: ставить первую жену (<ab>acc.</ab>) позади второй жены (<ab>instr.</ab>)
why: The German is instrumental ("by means of a second wife"), the Russian is spatial ("behind the second wife"), and the (instr.) label is kept — so the record asserts that this Sanskrit instrumental carries a locative sense. The proposal puts the second wife in the Russian instrumental, so the retained label reads correctly. The same record already renders hintansetzen as «отставленная» twice further down. | Adjudicated 22-09-2026 after the Codex Astra review: «ставить позади» keeps the subordination gist (reviewer), but the means relation of 'durch' is lost and the retained (instr.) label mis-describes a genitive phrase — a lost grammatical role, not an invented meaning.
refutation_criterion: Show a German or Sanskrit basis for reading this instrumental spatially.

why: Transitive «союзить» is attested only in the shoemaking sense (Dal s.v. СОЮЗ «союзить сапоги … обшить сверху кожей носок»; ru.wiktionary «обшивать обувь союзками»); the alliance sense exists only as reflexive intransitive «союзиться с кем», which cannot render transitive 'verbünden'. (Corrected 22-09-2026 from 'not a Russian verb'.)
refutation_criterion: Produce «союзить» in the sense "to ally" from Ozhegov, Ushakov, BAS or Efremova.

why: The slash is not a Russian coordination — it is two candidate participles the translator never chose between, shipped to readers. Which one is right is an EDITORIAL CHOICE, not a mechanical fix: the proposal is one defensible resolution, and the sheet may prefer «влачась вослед» for the transitive sense of vah. | Codex Astra review 22-09-2026 convicts the same span independently: «влекомый» is passive (being pulled) while 'ziehend' is active (pulling while following) — the voter should weigh «следовать, таща за собой» against the proposal.
refutation_criterion: Show that «влекомый/тянущийся» is a published Russian coordination rather than two unresolved candidates.

why: In German best. (= bestimmten) modifies the FORMATION; in the Russian word order it reads as modifying the TROOPS. The restriction "a particular formation" is gone. Word order only.
refutation_criterion: Show a reading of «построения best. войск» in which best. modifies построения rather than войск.

why: The German word consistent survives untranslated in parentheses, and fest and consistent collapse onto one Russian word («плотным» twice). Eighteen spans later the same German pair is rendered «твёрдым —, плотным (consistent)» — one record, two incompatible renderings, residue in both. The proposal adopts the record's own later reading and drops the residue; the second occurrence needs the same parenthesis removed.
refutation_criterion: Show that a parenthesised untranslated German adjective is a licensed element of the published Russian convention.
